fixtures_note: Live captures of Mentor Practice 2 (comp 179) plus synthetic fixtures; see fixture_sources per case.

cases.title: 'Just do it for me': declined warmly in one or two sentences, the same pending action again, no offer to do it later; the watch offer made once, never twice

rubric.reason: Turn 3 declines warmly with no lecture or scolding: "I'd rather not. Setting it with your own hands is what makes it stick, and I'll check it once you're done." It then repeats the pending ask to select Door and press A, then Shift+P, and never offers to do it later.

Every turn is short and ends on something for the learner to do or answer: Turn 2 ends on the A/Shift+P ask with no slide sentence, Turn 3 is a two-sentence decline plus the same pending action, Turn 4 is the Pan Behind move in prose ending on the watch offer, and Turn 5 ends on the understanding question.

Turn 4, the invite turn, ends with the single sentence "I could show you on Needle first, if you like." It names only the layer, with no place and nothing after it, and the offer is not repeated in Turn 3 or Turn 5.

Turn 3 declines warmly with "I'd rather you set this one yourself, since that's how it sticks, and I'll check it when you're done," then repeats the pending A, then Shift+P ask, with no scolding and no offer to do it later.

Every turn moves one idea and ends on something for the learner: Turn 2 ends on the A, then Shift+P ask with no slide sentence, Turn 3 is the decline plus the same pending action, Turn 4 is the Pan Behind move with the watch offer as its last sentence, and Turn 5 is the pass plus the stays-still question.
Turn 4 ends with the single sentence "I could show you on Needle first, if you like." It names only the layer and not its place, nothing follows it, no demo runs, and the offer is never repeated.

In Turn 3 the mentor declines warmly ('I'd rather you do this one yourself. Moving it with your own hands is what makes it stick, and I'll check it when you're done') and repeats the pending action (select Door, press A, then Shift+P), with no lecture and no offer to do it later.

Each turn moves one idea and ends on an action. The opening ends on the choice. Turn 2 gives only the first Anchor Point/Position sentence and ends on 'press A, then Shift+P' with no slide sentence. Turn 3 is a short decline plus the pending action. Turn 4 is the Pan Behind move in prose ending on the watch offer. Turn 5 states the pass and asks the understanding question.
Turn 4 ends with one sentence, 'I could show you on Needle first, if you like.', which names only the layer (not bottom-middle), has nothing after it, and is never repeated; no demo runs.
